children.text: Use the classical analogue \(\dot{\mathbf L}=\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B\), \(\boldsymbol\mu=-\gamma\mathbf L\), with γ>0. All frequencies in this problem are angular frequencies. A frame S′ rotates about z at +ω, with axes coincident with laboratory axes at t=0. The derivative rule is \((d\mathbf A/dt)_{lab}=(d\mathbf A/dt)_{rot}+\omega\hat z\times\mathbf A\). In part C an ensemble has Nup+Ndown=N and axial magnetization M=(Nup−Ndown)μ=Nμz. Initially all moments point along +z. The later measurement thought experiment uses its stated uncertainty estimate Δpx Δx≳ħ and its convention |μx|=|μz|=γħ.
Prove that |μ| is constant for any magnetic field. For stationary B show that its angle with μ is constant.
For B=B0 zhat find ω0 and its precession sense.
Show that \((d\boldsymbol\mu/dt)_{rot}=-\gamma\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B_{eff}\), and find Beff.
For static B=B0 zhat find the signed rotating-frame precession Δ in terms of ω0 and ω.
Add b(t)=b[cos(ωt)xhat+sin(ωt)yhat]. Derive the rotating-frame precession speed Ω.
Instead add b[cos(ωt)xhat−sin(ωt)yhat]. Find Beff in S′ and its time average.
Apply B=B0 zhat+2b cos(ω0t)xhat, with b≪B0 and ω=ω0=γB0. Show the approximate effective field and find Ω.
Find the angle α between the moment and the resonant effective field and prove M(t)=Nμ cos(Ωt).
Find and plot Pup(t),Pdown(t) on the same axes.

statement.text:
Physics of Spin
Use the classical analogue \(\dot{\mathbf L}=\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B\), \(\boldsymbol\mu=-\gamma\mathbf L\), with γ>0. All frequencies in this problem are angular frequencies. A frame S′ rotates about z at +ω, with axes coincident with laboratory axes at t=0. The derivative rule is \((d\mathbf A/dt)_{lab}=(d\mathbf A/dt)_{rot}+\omega\hat z\times\mathbf A\). In part C an ensemble has Nup+Ndown=N and axial magnetization M=(Nup−Ndown)μ=Nμz. Initially all moments point along +z. The later measurement thought experiment uses its stated uncertainty estimate Δpx Δx≳ħ and its convention |μx|=|μz|=γħ.
a.1. Conserved moment and angle
Prove that |μ| is constant for any magnetic field. For stationary B show that its angle with μ is constant.
a.2. Larmor frequency
For B=B0 zhat find ω0 and its precession sense.
b.1. Effective rotating-frame field
Show that \((d\boldsymbol\mu/dt)_{rot}=-\gamma\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B_{eff}\), and find Beff.
b.2. Detuning in rotating frame
For static B=B0 zhat find the signed rotating-frame precession Δ in terms of ω0 and ω.
b.3. Co-rotating applied field
Add b(t)=b[cos(ωt)xhat+sin(ωt)yhat]. Derive the rotating-frame precession speed Ω.
b.4. Counter-rotating field
Instead add b[cos(ωt)xhat−sin(ωt)yhat]. Find Beff in S′ and its time average.
c.1. Rotating-wave approximation
Apply B=B0 zhat+2b cos(ω0t)xhat, with b≪B0 and ω=ω0=γB0. Show the approximate effective field and find Ω.
c.2. Magnetization oscillation
Find the angle α between the moment and the resonant effective field and prove M(t)=Nμ cos(Ωt).
c.3. Rabi populations
Find and plot Pup(t),Pdown(t) on the same axes.
d.1. Resolving the spin beams

A silver beam travels along −y. A first z-biased Stern-Gerlach region and screen SC1 at distance D prepare +z moments. The screen opening has width Δx. The next x-biased region exerts Fx=μx C, with μx=±γħ. If the flight time after SC1 is t, show the condition needed to distinguish the two x beams.
d.2. Loss of axial-spin information
The second region has Bx=B0+Cx. Show that resolving μx causes a large spread in precession angle and destroys the prepared μz information in this model.

children.text: \(\dot{\boldsymbol\mu}=-\gamma\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B\). Therefore \(d\mu^2/dt=2\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\dot{\boldsymbol\mu}=0\). If B is fixed, \(d(\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B)/dt=0\) also. Both magnitudes and their dot product are fixed, so the angle is fixed.
\(\dot{\boldsymbol\mu}=\gamma\mathbf B\times\boldsymbol\mu\), so the angular velocity vector is +γB0 zhat and \(\omega_0=\gamma B_0\).

Subtract frame rotation from the lab derivative. Since \(-\omega\hat z\times\boldsymbol\mu=\omega\boldsymbol\mu\times\hat z\), the effective field is \(\mathbf B_{eff}=\mathbf B-(\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}\).
The signed axial angular velocity is \(\Delta=\omega_0-\omega\). Its nonnegative speed is |Δ|. The sign records the direction of relative rotation.
The rotating field is constant along x′. Thus \(\mathbf B_{eff}=b\hat x^{\prime}+(B_0-\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}\) and \[\Omega=\gamma\sqrt{(B_0-\omega/\gamma)^2+b^2}.\]

The field rotates at −2ω in S′: \[\mathbf B_{eff}=(B_0-\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}+b[\cos2\omega t\,\hat x^{\prime}-\sin2\omega t\,\hat y^{\prime}].\] Averaging a full rotation leaves only \((B_0-\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}\).

Split the linear oscillation into equal co- and counter-rotating fields. On resonance the static axial effective field cancels. The counter-rotating piece oscillates at 2ω0, much faster than γb, so its leading average vanishes. Thus \(\mathbf B_{eff}\simeq b\hat x^{\prime}\), \(\Omega=\gamma b\).
Initially μ is along z and Beff is along x′, so α=π/2 and remains fixed. Rotation about x′ gives \(\mu_z=\mu\cos\Omega t\). Since z′=z, the measured axial magnetization is \(M=N\mu\cos\Omega t\).
Solve Pup+Pdown=1 and Pup−Pdown=M/(Nμ): \[P_{up}=\cos^2(\Omega t/2),\qquad P_{down}=\sin^2(\Omega t/2).\] They are complementary, have period 2π/Ω, and exchange populations at t=π/Ω. At t=0 Pup=1.

Uncertainty gives transverse velocity spread \(\Delta v_x\gtrsim\hbar/(m\Delta x)\), so width grows by roughly ħt/(mΔx). Opposite forces separate the beam centres by \(d_x=|\mu_x|Ct^2/m\). Resolution requires \[|\mu_x|C\Delta x\,t/\hbar\gg1.\]

Field variation is ΔB=CΔx, giving \(\Delta\omega=\gamma C\Delta x=(|\mu_x|/\hbar)C\Delta x\). The resolution condition therefore implies Δωt≫1. The ensemble acquires a broad spread of rotations around x, so its original definite z projection is lost. This gives the intended incompatibility argument under the stated semiclassical estimate.

solution.text:
Physics of Spin
a.1. Conserved moment and angle
\(\dot{\boldsymbol\mu}=-\gamma\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B\). Therefore \(d\mu^2/dt=2\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\dot{\boldsymbol\mu}=0\). If B is fixed, \(d(\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B)/dt=0\) also. Both magnitudes and their dot product are fixed, so the angle is fixed.
a.2. Larmor frequency
\(\dot{\boldsymbol\mu}=\gamma\mathbf B\times\boldsymbol\mu\), so the angular velocity vector is +γB0 zhat and \(\omega_0=\gamma B_0\).
b.1. Effective rotating-frame field
Subtract frame rotation from the lab derivative. Since \(-\omega\hat z\times\boldsymbol\mu=\omega\boldsymbol\mu\times\hat z\), the effective field is \(\mathbf B_{eff}=\mathbf B-(\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}\).
b.2. Detuning in rotating frame
The signed axial angular velocity is \(\Delta=\omega_0-\omega\). Its nonnegative speed is |Δ|. The sign records the direction of relative rotation.
b.3. Co-rotating applied field
The rotating field is constant along x′. Thus \(\mathbf B_{eff}=b\hat x^{\prime}+(B_0-\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}\) and \[\Omega=\gamma\sqrt{(B_0-\omega/\gamma)^2+b^2}.\]
b.4. Counter-rotating field
The field rotates at −2ω in S′: \[\mathbf B_{eff}=(B_0-\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}+b[\cos2\omega t\,\hat x^{\prime}-\sin2\omega t\,\hat y^{\prime}].\] Averaging a full rotation leaves only \((B_0-\omega/\gamma)\hat z^{\prime}\).
c.1. Rotating-wave approximation
Split the linear oscillation into equal co- and counter-rotating fields. On resonance the static axial effective field cancels. The counter-rotating piece oscillates at 2ω0, much faster than γb, so its leading average vanishes. Thus \(\mathbf B_{eff}\simeq b\hat x^{\prime}\), \(\Omega=\gamma b\).
c.2. Magnetization oscillation
Initially μ is along z and Beff is along x′, so α=π/2 and remains fixed. Rotation about x′ gives \(\mu_z=\mu\cos\Omega t\). Since z′=z, the measured axial magnetization is \(M=N\mu\cos\Omega t\).
c.3. Rabi populations
Solve Pup+Pdown=1 and Pup−Pdown=M/(Nμ): \[P_{up}=\cos^2(\Omega t/2),\qquad P_{down}=\sin^2(\Omega t/2).\] They are complementary, have period 2π/Ω, and exchange populations at t=π/Ω. At t=0 Pup=1.
d.1. Resolving the spin beams
Uncertainty gives transverse velocity spread \(\Delta v_x\gtrsim\hbar/(m\Delta x)\), so width grows by roughly ħt/(mΔx). Opposite forces separate the beam centres by \(d_x=|\mu_x|Ct^2/m\). Resolution requires \[|\mu_x|C\Delta x\,t/\hbar\gg1.\]
d.2. Loss of axial-spin information
Field variation is ΔB=CΔx, giving \(\Delta\omega=\gamma C\Delta x=(|\mu_x|/\hbar)C\Delta x\). The resolution condition therefore implies Δωt≫1. The ensemble acquires a broad spread of rotations around x, so its original definite z projection is lost. This gives the intended incompatibility argument under the stated semiclassical estimate.
